title: Canonical twist comparison on a generated Proj chart
statement: Let $A$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring, $T$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $\psi:A\to\Gamma_*(T,L)$ a graded ring homomorphism [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. Let $U(\psi)$ be the union of the nonvanishing opens [def-sc-section-generating-locus] of $\psi(f)$ for positive-degree homogeneous $f$, and let $r:U(\psi)\to\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj] be the canonical morphism. If $d\ge1$ and $V\subseteq U(\psi)$ is an open subscheme on which the sections $\psi(A_d)$ generate $L^{\otimes d}|_V$, then the canonical graded comparison $\theta_d:(r|_V)^*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Proj}(A)}(d)\to L^{\otimes d}|_V$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] [def-pc-module-pullback] [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is an isomorphism. It is the unique comparison carrying the pullback of each homogeneous section $a\in A_d$ to $\psi(a)|_V$, and the comparisons obtained in different positive degrees are compatible with the graded multiplication maps.

source.place: Tag 01NK (lemma-invertible-map-into-proj), graded comparison θ and final assertion; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), construction and uniqueness in a common positive degree.

proof.text: Write $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ and $s_f=\psi(f)$ for homogeneous $f$ of positive degree $e$. The canonical $r$ and graded comparison in the statement are obtained by extending $\psi$ after inverting $f$ on $T_{s_f}$. Explicitly, in degree $m\ge0$ this extension sends $b/f^q\in(A_f)_m$, with $b\in A_{m+qe}$, to $\psi(b)/s_f^q$. Here division means the inverse of tensoring with the generator $s_f^q$; degree zero gives the functions map defining $r$ on this chart. The formula is forced by $f\cdot f^{-1}=1$ and the prescribed image of every $b/1$. The twisting-sheaf definition identifies these fractions with chart sections and identifies the global section $b$ with $b/1$. In particular $\theta_m(r^*b)=\psi(b)$ for $b\in A_m$.

source.place: Tag 01NK (lemma-invertible-map-into-proj), graded-localization construction and uniqueness; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local bases and their overlap comparison

proof.text: The opens $W_a=V\cap T_{\psi(a)}$, for $a\in A_d$, cover $V$. Indeed at any $x\in V$ trivialize the invertible module $L^{\otimes d}$ and write the germs of $\psi(a)$ as coefficients $c_a$ times its basis. Generation says that a finite sum $\sum h_ac_a=1$ in the local ring $\mathcal O_{T,x}$. If all $c_a$ lay in its maximal ideal so would this sum; hence one is a unit. The corresponding section generates on a neighbourhood of $x$, exactly membership in its generating locus. Tensor powers are locally rank one because tensoring a local basis of $L$ with itself gives a basis. No finite subcover or quasi-compactness is used.

source.place: Tag 01NK (lemma-invertible-map-into-proj), graded-localization construction and uniqueness; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local bases and their overlap comparison

proof.text: For $a\in A_d$, multiplication by $a$ gives an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{D_+(a)}\to\mathcal O_P(d)|_{D_+(a)}$. To see this on a basis of subopens $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(a)$, use the twisting-sheaf chart formula: the map is $(A_g)_0\to(A_g)_d$, $u\mapsto au$. The element $a$ is invertible in $A_g$, with inverse homogeneous of degree $-d$, so $v\mapsto a^{-1}v$ is its inverse. For completeness, a relation $g^N=ca$ gives $a^{-1}=c/g^N$ of degree $-d$. Localization restrictions commute with multiplication by both $a$ and $a^{-1}$, so these inverse maps define inverse sheaf maps. The global degree-$d$ section $a$ is precisely this basis section, since it restricts to $a/1$.

source.place: Tag 01NK (lemma-invertible-map-into-proj), graded-localization construction and uniqueness; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local bases and their overlap comparison

proof.text: Restrict to $W_a$. The canonical chart construction has $r(W_a)\subseteq D_+(a)$. Pullback of the inverse maps of Step 3 again gives inverse maps. In the tensor definition of pullback the basis is $1\otimes a$, since $\mathcal O_{W_a}\otimes_{r^{-1}\mathcal O_P}r^{-1}\mathcal O_P\simeq\mathcal O_{W_a}$ by $u\otimes v\mapsto u\,r^\sharp(v)$, inverse $u\mapsto u\otimes1$. Meanwhile the nonvanishing-section trivialization applied to $L^{\otimes d}$ identifies $L^{\otimes d}|_{W_a}$ with $\mathcal O_{W_a}$ through the basis $\psi(a)$. Step 1 shows that $\theta_d$ sends $1\otimes a$ to $\psi(a)$, so in these bases it is the identity. It is therefore invertible on every $W_a$. Its local inverses agree on intersections because they invert the same map, and glue by the sheaf condition to a global inverse on $V$.

source.place: Tag 01NK (lemma-invertible-map-into-proj), graded-localization construction and uniqueness; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local bases and their overlap comparison

proof.text: If another $\mathcal O_V$-linear comparison carries every pulled-back $a\in A_d$ to $\psi(a)|_V$, its restriction to $W_a$ agrees with $\theta_d$ on the basis $1\otimes a$ of Step 4. Linearity makes the two maps agree on every section on every subopen of $W_a$. Since the $W_a$ cover $V$, the sheaf condition makes the maps equal on $V$. This proves uniqueness among all comparisons, not just among isomorphisms. For empty $V$ all these sheaves have exactly one section on the empty open and the same argument gives the unique isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01NK (lemma-invertible-map-into-proj), graded-localization construction and uniqueness; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local bases and their overlap comparison

proof.text:
Finally check graded multiplication directly, without assuming multiplication of Proj twists is globally invertible. On a canonical chart $T_{s_f}$, take fractions $b/f^p$ and $c/f^q$ of degrees $m$ and $n$. Multiplication of the shifted modules is multiplication in $A_f$, hence their product is $bc/f^{p+q}$. The formula of Step 1 gives
$$\frac{\psi(bc)}{s_f^{p+q}}=\frac{\psi(b)}{s_f^p}\,\frac{\psi(c)}{s_f^q},$$
because $\psi$ is a graded ring map and multiplication in the section ring is tensor multiplication. The tensor definition of pullback extends this identity bilinearly to coefficients in $\mathcal O_T$; the sheaf tensor product is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor, so pure-tensor equality gives equality of the two sheaf maps. The charts cover $U(\psi)$, so the equality holds there and after restriction to any common open. In particular the isomorphisms in any positive generated degrees are the components of this same multiplication-compatible comparison, as required.
